utterances.text: This was never so and it is difficult for me to presume that something of the sort would be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were also shown by Mr. Harmon an entry concerning the sending of 3- to 5.000 members of the VRS to Lika, purporting to be the words of President Milosevic, and you replied to the best of your knowledge that two battalions or up to 1.000 men were sent. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it known to you whether anybody else -- anybody was brought to account or castigated that only 1.000 and not 3- to 5.000 men were sent after this conversation with President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was held responsible, neither did I resent that because I simply knew that they did not have the men available.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us deal with a number of issues concerning your replies concerning the documents on the Drina War Plan. Answering Mr. Harmon - and that would be page 31 of LiveNote of the 2nd of December [as interpreted] - you said that with respect to the new Drina Plan, unit war plans remained intact because, as you said, this next step for the implementation of that plan never materialised. Do you recall that answer?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us here, as a military expert, what would be the definition of co-ordinated action by units?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Co-ordinated action is aligning the actions against the target in time and place and by type of manoeuvre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Units which are carrying out a co-ordinating action, irrespective of which army or several armies at the time, what would be their mutual relationship?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Co-ordinated action is organised among units of the same level. The term "co-ordinated action," Mr. Lukic, is referring to combat actions. This is something I dealt with in my post-grad studies and this is a very precise military term.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For units to act in co-ordinated fashion, what is necessary to have an operation carried out in co-ordinated action in terms of preparations for that?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the basic idea of the commander, a co-ordinated action plan is drafted, you go out in the field, commander performs a reconnaissance, and then the plan is tied to a certain area, facilities, lines on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please define the term "co-ordinated action," and that is in the transcript, 47, row 7. Could you please repeat your definition of co-ordinated action. There are certain discrepancy in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is alignment of actions by target, time, place, and manoeuvre. These are my exact words.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show on the screen Exhibit P215. That would be the Drina directive. I would like you, please, to show us page 9 in B/C/S and 9 in English. I'm mistaken with respect to both pages. Please, can we go back one page in B/C/S for a moment. Let's keep the English page here and then we will turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the paragraph headed: "Task of the armed forces. "1. Yugoslav Army." And let's go -- let's turn both pages in B/C/S and English. There is a portion of a sentence that I'd like to comment -- or elicit comment from the witness about. Your Honours, the relevant portion in English is the large paragraph starting with: "Upon completing mobilisation ..." General, I'm going to read the beginning of the sentence on the preceding page, which continues on this page. "Upon completing the mobilisation, the main forces are used to organise the defence from the area of Hungary, Macedonia in the depth of the territory, and Albania and part of the forces to be used for co-ordinated action with SVK to dominate the line Josipovic-Mikanovci-Samac and use VRS to destroy the enemy forces in the Drina valley to take control over eastern Herzegovina and the left bank of the Neretva river at the Mostar-Neum section." I believe I have trouble with the English translation, but let me ask you this: This is the task for the VJ pursuant to this Drina Plan, and it says -- said that in offensive actions they have to co-ordinate their actions with SVK to -- for that to be possible, what needs to be done beforehand to have this joint action by the VJ and the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is necessary is insert into the war plans of the SVK and the VJ in the next step of the preparations of war plans, first of all, to plan and draw on the map the tasks of units and prepare a separate co-ordinated action or joint action plan, and then go out in the field with unit commanders that are supposed to act in that designated area and precise everything out on the ground, and that would be the implementation of a plan as a plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go, please, to the next page in B/C/S and the next page in English. Your Honours, I'm going to read out the first sentence of this paragraph where mention of SVK is made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "SVK -- the SVK with VRS reinforcements and in co-ordination action with POd and special VJ forces ..." et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I've been trying to follow what you're reading. I can't see. Which paragraph is that one which starts with the VJ or SVK?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that the English translation doesn't match what I read out in Serbian. It's the first paragraph under the title: "The Serbian Army of the Krajina."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the third paragraph in both Serbian and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read out the paragraph once more in Serbian -- or maybe you, General, read out this first paragraph first because of the abbreviations.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Serbian Army of the Krajina with VRS reinforcements and in co-ordinated action with forward detachments of special VJ forces is to prevent any surprises ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Special forces of the VJ are mentioned here. General, do you know whether at any time anybody contacted you about the implementation of what is said in this document about the co-ordinated action of your army?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One other brief comment. On the same page in the B/C/S version and in the following page of the English version, the use of anti-aircraft defence and air force is mentioned, and I'll read out the first sentence: "With RV and PVO forces in co-ordinated action with ground forces PVO," that is, anti-aircraft defence, "organised a joint anti-aircraft system with the focus on the protection of the armed forces, features, and most significant administrative and military and industrial centres in the RS, RSK, and FRY." Was a single anti-aircraft defence system ever established?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, all these facts that you have spoken about with regard to the implementation of this plan, what did all this tell you, that nobody contacted you from the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are requested to please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, given the fact that you didn't contact anybody in the VJ or the VRS concerning the subsequent development of this plan, what did that tell you at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to object. I'm not sure I understand the question. Whether he didn't contact anybody. I'm not sure what that -- I'm not sure I don't comprehend the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed it doesn't make much sense couched like that. The previous question, which now Mr. Lukic has departed from, was given that -- well, General, all these facts that you have spoken about with regards to the implementation of this plan, what did all this tell you that nobody contacted you from -- and then you didn't finish that sentence. Now, I don't know whether you want the witness to tell you what it tells him that he did not contact anybody. What can tell him anything is that nobody contacted him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what I wanted to hear from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except that the two questions are different, sir. The first question was -- yeah -- I think that is what --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, what did it mean to you, I mean the fact that you weren't in contact from anybody -- with anybody from the VJ and the VRS concerning the further implementation of this Drina Plan?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the Drina Plan would never be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive at that conclusion? And I'm referring to November 1993 when the Drina Plan was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even then I thought that it would be very difficult to implement the Drina Plan. If you want to know why, I can state my reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you when you realised that the Drina Plan would never be implemented. When did you arrive at that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when the commanders - the officers in charge in the VJ and in the VRS - refused -- or rather, failed to arrive from the areas where according to that plan their units should have been and where the tasks of those units should have been elaborated in more detail. It was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If this document was adopted in November 1993 -- November 1993 anyway, when did you expect them to arrive to do that?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All documents of the war plan at all levels of planning should have been completed within two or three weeks. That is a realistic dead-line for making such a plan at all levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this a convenient moment for the break, Your Honours? I'll have a few questions for the witness left, because I'm about to move on to another topic and only a few minutes are left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P2923 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a document that Mr. Harmon showed to us during his examination. It's your order dated 28 August 1993, where it is mentioned that you ordered for -- ordered that action against targets in Osijek and Vinkovci be planned and in case of artillery action also against Zagreb. Do you remember that Mr. Harmon put it to you that Zagreb is singled out and not mentioned with the rest of the towns that constitute military targets? So let me first ask you: What does "planning" mean and what was the purpose of this order?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the artillery, planning means determining all three co-ordinates of a particular target, not as an object in space but I mean a particular target. Then decide on a type of weapons and the type of fire to be opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know which targets in the city of Zagreb were selected to be taken action against?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely for any of these towns. They may have been targets that are the headquarters of the highest state authorities in charge of the army or targets of the police or military forces used against us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have finished with this document. Yesterday Mr. Harmon showed or put to you the allegations in the court decision from 1995 by a Croatian court sentencing you to 20 years of imprisonment because of the shelling of some towns in Croatia. Here's my question to you: Apart from the occasion when you gave an interview to the OTP of this Tribunal, did you ever meet any representatives of the OTP; and if so, where and when?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had several encounters with investigators of the ICTY even at the time when they were banned from entering Serbia, as I said. To the best of my recollection, in September 2001 in the building used by the Tribunal in Belgrade Mr. Savo Strbac and I met Ms. Carla del Ponte. Her head of office was there, I believe her name was -- she was later held responsible for contempt of court here --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That doesn't matter. But what was the topic of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Carla del Ponte asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I'm not sure how this relates to my cross-examination, a meeting with Carla del Ponte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, that's the answer that was given. That was not the question put.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, so I object to that continued questioning on this because it has no bearing on my cross-examination. The question that starts out is -- relates to a question I asked in respect of charges that -- a conviction against General Novakovic that was entered in a Croatian court in 1995. We have now drifted to a conversation that General Novakovic had with Carla del Ponte. It is not relevant, as far as I can see, nor is it particularly responsive to the question, nor, Your Honour, does it relate -- have any relationship to my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it relates to the cross-examination and has a direct bearing on what Mr. Harmon put to the witness concerning his conviction by Croatian court. That is why I want to ask him what information he received from the OTP concerning these particular matters. Since Mr. Harmon tried to impeach the witness by asking these questions, I want to ask the witness what information he had concerning what he was charged with. And it is -- I believe that is relevant for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That last sentence you make is a question you can put to the witness. The rest is -- has nothing to do with the crimes in -- alleged in Croatia. You can ask him what information he has about the alleged crimes, but the conversation with members of the OTP -- he was not charged by the members of this OTP in Croatia. And I guess that's why Mr. Harmon is standing. It would be perfectly correct to ask him what information he received from anybody about the allegations in Croatia, and if he received any information from Carla del Ponte so be it. But you can't introduce the topic by directing him to OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, you heard what kind of answer we're trying to elicit from you, namely, what kind of information you received concerning the charges Mr. Harmon spoke to you about and in -- and the link between you and those charges.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke directly to Ms. del Ponte about what the Croats, the Croatian judiciary, charges me with and about the information they passed on to the OTP of this Tribunal. And I said to her if she considers me responsible for anything, that I would be willing to go to The Hague immediately because I have no reason to hide nor did I do anything wrong. Ms. del Ponte said to me that she doesn't have anything against me, anything to charge me with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll refer to the questions asked to you today by Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see what was admitted today as Exhibit P2927.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon showed you this today. It's entitled a regular combat report which you sent to certain addressees, among others to the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ. It is dated 11 May 1995, as you see in the letterhead --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I think this is the problem with this document. It is dated the -- there are two dates, one date in the Serbian-language version and one date in the English version. So I believe Mr. Lukic pointed out that discrepancy earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. Obviously it's been uploaded in different versions. I would like to ask my learned colleague, the version that he showed to the witness is the one dated the 3rd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the version in English, but the thing is that the B/C/S is dated differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think I can assist in this matter, Your Honour. If we could have B/C/S version -- B/C/S language page 2 of XN -- I'm sorry, P2927 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- if we could have B/C/S page 2, that will resolve the dilemma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine. The B/C/S is dated the 11th. The English is dated the 3rd. Is it 3rd now? It was 11th just now a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They have been reconciled now, the two exhibits, Your Honour, on the monitor. They're both the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But how did that date of the 11th change?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can't say that. I believe that the exhibit that was put on that showed the 11th of May was a different page in a larger document. I can only speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Go on, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am not absolutely satisfied with the explanation. Both these pages purport to be first pages of a document. That's why they've got a date on them and a heading. Either -- if this one dated the 3rd of May is the original of which the English version is a translation, then the one dated the 11th should then be - what is the word? - what is the opposite of uploading? Must be offloaded from -- must be offloaded because then it -- I suspect that is a different exhibit completely, and I don't think it has been tendered. It came in by mistake. The intention was to tender the one dated the 3rd, but we were given something wrong. So that one must come off.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let it be offloaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because that is the document that the witness testified about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, General, now we have in front of us a document dated the 3rd of May, 1995. I'm going to ask you the same question as a couple of minutes ago. What does this date trigger memory of, what associations you have with respect to this date and the days around it?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Croatian offensive in the area of Western Slavonia was under way in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at D164 and have it brought on the screen. What was the name of that operation, General?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said the Croatian offensive, that would be page 58, line 25.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The code-name is Flash or Blesak and it's still known under that sobriquet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're going to see the map that you already saw and on which you indicated certain things for our benefit. When it does appear, I would like to ask you to draw two things on that map. But let us wait for a second for it to appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could zoom in on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And with the usher's help, Witness, I'm going to ask you to indicate two things on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you, usher, would please assist the General, to assist General Novakovic, although I see that the General has become very skilful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please indicate on this map the areas where you were and where Operation Pauk on the 3rd of May, 1995, while it unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the spot, sir, indicated by 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And please indicate where the Croatian army aggression labelled Flash was carried out in that period.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the area marked by the number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will move to tender this map into evidence before it disappears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The map shall be given -- the marked portion of the map shall be given Exhibit D00444. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, Operation Flash, this operation of the Croatian army and the developments of that time in the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, did they have any implications on the security of the FRY and was there any need to inform Chief of General Staff of the VJ of such events?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, such an operation of -- at such large scale in the vicinity would be something that not only the Chief of Staff of the VJ but the Chief of Staff of the Hungarian army would have to be informed about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's take a look at a document which has been XN32, the designation given by the OTP to that document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: XN320 or 320.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not a document which is on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon -- Mr. Lukic, when was XN320 tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That document, XN320, has not been tendered. The OTP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, but when did the OTP put it on the screen? I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not upload it. I referred to it because the OTP introduced that document into the e-court. That document has not been shown to the Bench so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this -- I just wanted to confirm, this document was not shown to the witness and I don't know what its relationship is to the cross-examination. And perhaps Mr. Lukic would be in a position to inform us how this relates to the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like then to ask Mr. Novakovic to step out of the courtroom for me to be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, will you please give us a bit of a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see, by its form it is the same type of document as P2527 but the date is the 1st of July, 1995, whereby Pauk command delivers this document exclusively to Mr. Jovica Stanisic. It's not been addressed to the General Staff of the VJ, and I would like to refute Mr. Harmon's thesis using this document in respect of the periods of reporting and delivery of reports, whereby Mr. Harmon tried to prove to Mr. Novakovic that he did deliver regular reports to Mr. Stanisic -- sorry, Mr. Perisic, and this does follow from cross-examination directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that this refutes the testimony, but I'll leave it to Mr. Lukic to determine. The witness said he delivered reports, regular combat reports, once a week to General Perisic. That was his evidence as I recall it, so I'm not sure this refutes that proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, that was the evidence. But the proposition put to him was that he made regular reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, I agree, Your Honour. I asked him if he made -- how often he made regular combat report submissions to General Perisic and my recollection is he said once a week. This is a regular combat report. It doesn't mean that -- I don't want to say more. It's up to -- let's proceed, Your Honour. I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Call the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document, General, please, and then I'm going to ask you a couple of questions. Do you recognise your signature here?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This purports to be, as it's entitled, regular combat report by Pauk command dated the 1st of July, 1995, and in this case it is addressed to the attention of Mr. J. Stanisic. When Mr. Harmon asked you in his cross-examination about the regularity of delivering those combat reports to General Perisic, you said that as far as you could remember you provided one such report once a week or from time to time. My question in this period why didn't you or did you continue to deliver reports to the General Staff of the VJ, namely, General Perisic, during that period?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my memory serves me, Mr. Lukic, throughout the duration of this operation we delivered reports to most of the people, as specified earlier when those reports were called up. I don't see this as a special case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I'm going to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I propose that we tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this shall be admitted as Exhibit D00445.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, towards the end of his cross-examination, asked you a number of questions about Mr. Ulemek, Mr. Medic, and asked you about their participation in Operation Pauk. You remember he showed you some footage dated 6th of April, 1995, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please bring on the screen P2783. I'm not sure whether this document is still under seal. The seal may have been removed, but if not then we'll have to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, are you able to guide us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These are excerpts from General Mladic's diary. The first one that was disclosed to us about one and a half years ago and which the OTP introduced into their evidence towards the end of their case. Could we please turn to B/C/S page 10 and English page 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic inform me whether this is a reflection of a meeting that Mr. -- General Novakovic attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I do not see that it has been stated that General Novakovic attended that meeting. I'd like to ask General Novakovic about something else in relation with the relationship Ulemek and Medic had. I cannot see from this entry whether General Novakovic attended that meeting at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- Your Honour, perhaps a question could be put to the General before he's shown a document. If the question is: What is the relationship between Ulemek and somebody else, if he knows? That's a question that can be put to him without the use of a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not want to dwell on these issues. I would like to ask a specific question which follows from the allegations in this diary which relate to Mr. Novakovic in the period while Ulemek was present in the territory, as shown to the General by Mr. Harmon. I'm going to discuss an entry in this diary which has direct relationship with Mr. Harmon's questions put to the General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You know, there is a practice that has taken place in this Tribunal which makes life very difficult. According to my understanding, before a document is shown to a witness you've got to lay a foundation for that document. In this Tribunal documents are just put on and then say: Okay, fine, I'm going to ask a question. And by the time the question is asked, the very purpose of not showing the document before the foundation is laid is undermined and it becomes water under the bridge because now the witness has seen the document anyway. And this exchange that you have now had with Mr. Harmon confuses me. First of all, Mr. Harmon did not object to anything. He just asked: Can I be told whether the witness attended this meeting. Now, that's not an objection. That's not any reason why a question should not be put. You gave an explanation of why you want to put the document to the witness. I still don't understand why, you know. And it would be helpful indeed, as Mr. Harmon suggests, if questions can be put to the witness. Let's hear what they are, let's hear what the relevance is, and if in the course of asking questions you either want to jog the memory of the witness or you want to develop the point on your questions, then you can show him the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he asked General Novakovic the question and asked about his departure to Belgrade with Ulemek --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ask those questions to the witness, deal with those questions, develop a foundation for showing the witness the document, Mr. Lukic. You see, you're explaining to us. We will follow you if you deal with the questions that were asked in cross-examination and you put them to the witness. We will understand what you are doing. And if you want to show him a document, either in confirmation or in -- refuting what you are dealing with, then we will understand why the document is coming on the screen. But when you don't show him the paper before you've asked the questions -- am I being difficult?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you what you people make difficult for me. I don't know how to rule in what you're talking about. As I say, there is no objection; there is just a question. And now the following statements that Mr. Harmon made after asking about whether the witness attended this meeting suggest an objection. He hasn't said so expressly, but he shows dissatisfaction with you showing the witness this document, you know, before you have told us why you want to show him a document and before the Court can determine whether in fact you are entitled to show him the document or not, depending on the relevance of your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I've just received instructions and in line with these instructions I'm about to ask you the following question. In the spring of 1995 what kind of relationship was there in place between Jovica Stanisic and you as the commander of Pauk?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was not fully satisfied that I was in the position I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, why did Mr. Stanisic dislike the fact that you were in that position?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the basic reason was that I tried to think with my own head and take decisions based on what I hear from the people around me. And the gentleman who's been mentioned here, Mr. Ulemek, to my mind was in a position for which he was not fit. And I stated as much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please let us now look at this document. On the first page we see reference to a meeting that took place on the 30th of June, 1995, at the General Staff of the VJ with President Milosevic. And then in the second sentence we see: "I called FA," although I see on the English translation that this -- these initials are already expanded, but let me ask you anyway, General. Who did Mladic refer to when he -- with these initials, FA?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, so the record is clear, the question that I understood was who did Mladic refer to and Mladic is not obviously mentioned but President Milosevic is mentioned. And so I think the record is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- did anybody refer to Mladic, Mr. Harmon? I thought Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, at line 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, I'm with you. Who did Mladic refer to when he -- you meant Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant Mladic when he wrote the initials FA because this is Mladic's handwriting, and I don't believe that Milosevic actually uttered "FA." So I said "Mladic" because this is Mladic's diary. Sorry for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now we are with you, Mr. Lukic. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see pages 13 in both B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says here: "JS: My men should be given maximum consideration when an operation is planned. "I don't trust Mile Novakovic, at least in terms of expertise ..." General, at that time did you have information to this effect that Jovica Stanisic doesn't trust you as commander or didn't trust your activities in the Pauk operation with regard to Ulemek?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I felt that their relations weren't very close. That's what I knew. That Mr. Stanisic doubts my expertise, well that is something I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, you won't believe me, but I put it to you anyway: I'm done with my examination. Thank you once more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. -- oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, I also put it to you that you'll be surprised that I'm telling you that we are done with your testimony. We are so grateful you came here and testified before this Tribunal. You have been here for a long time and we thank you for your co-operation with the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down and travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow, Mr. President, I would like to thank you personally and the Trial Chamber for a correct and humane attitude, and that is the memory I carry home with me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Mr. Lukic. May the Chamber please move into open session. Sorry, we should have excused the witness in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have the next witness ready to appear in court on Monday and testify in accordance with the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then can we just deal with a minor housekeeping matter. Mr. Lukic, are you able to give an estimation of how much longer the Defence case is going to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that's something of interest to everybody, including myself. I would like to say immediately that it is the Defence's wish to finish as soon as possible. I cannot be very precise, but what I can say is that we are about to shorten our list of witnesses. And after the testimony of Mr. Novakovic, we will again eliminate some witnesses. I cannot be more precise than that because there are now some technical matters that must be resolved with regards to some important witnesses. I believe that we will know within two or three weeks, for which period we already have a list of witnesses. And then I will be in a position to be more precise as to the intended end of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let me put my question slightly differently to you. From a planning point of view, the Chamber would wish to have in its hands at least closing briefs before we go for the winter recess. Can you promise that we will -- we can achieve that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot, as much as I would like to. It is my desire to reach that goal, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we -- can the Chamber urge the parties, including the Prosecution, that we work towards that goal?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will certainly honour your request and do whatever is in my power to meet that -- to reach that objective. But although I don't want to go into great lengths, but I would like to illustrate some of the problems the Defence is up against so this fits into this topic that you have just broached. We are still working on some matters so we don't have additional matters that we don't have -- don't yet have a complete picture about. But in order for me to be more specific, we would have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We stand adjourned to Monday morning, 9.00, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.
